positions.meaning: your experiences and influences from approximately the previous 18 to 24 months
steps: 1 · The original card in this position
2 · Clarifier 1 · how it modifies the original card
positions.original:
1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · XVIII · The Moon, reversed

Past · 18–24 Months

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Pisces
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Pisces · Water

Number: 18

Eighteen enters uncertainty, where feeling and imagination need careful discernment. In The Moon, consider how this relates to uncertainty.

Emerging Clarity
Confusion
Projection

Position: Past · 18–24 Months — The Moon reversed. Looking across the previous 18 to 24 months, emerging clarity, confusion, projection may show an experience or influence that helped shape the present situation.

Something previously obscured may be coming into view, though anxiety can still distort it. Separate what you know, what you imagine and what remains uncertain before choosing your response.

Looking closer: A path runs between towers beneath the moon, with a dog, wolf and emerging crayfish. Familiar and instinctive responses meet at the edge of the unknown.
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · III · Three of Swords, reversed

Recovery may be beginning or hurt may be turning inward. Allow time and support, and distinguish forgiving yourself from pretending that the wound did not matter.

Astrology: Air · Swords · Air

Number: 3

Three develops expression, growth and the effects of working together. In Three of Swords, consider how this relates to sorrow.

Looking closer: Three swords pierce a heart beneath rain clouds, giving emotional pain a direct visual form.

Three of Swords (reversed) modifies The Moon (reversed).

In Past · 18–24 Months, the theme of recovery and held resentment changes how emerging clarity and confusion may be expressed, rather than strengthening or opposing it.

Read this way because Water and Air are neutral to each other.

With both cards reversed, look at what is being held back or resisted. As a Minor Arcana card, Three of Swords brings the Major theme down to a practical, everyday expression in thought, decisions and conflict.
positions.together:

Together in Past · 18–24 Months

Revision 1 · with Clarifier 1.

In the wider Seven-card V Reading spread, Past · 18–24 Months opens the reading; its neighbour is Present Time, Five of Cups (reversed), which reinforces The Moon (both are Water cards).

This is a perspective for reflection, not a fixed prediction.

positions.label: Present Time
positions.meaning: your present circumstances, including the period immediately surrounding today
positions.original:
Original Card · V · Five of Cups, reversed

Present Time

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Water · Cups
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Water · Cups · Water

Number: 5

Five disrupts an established pattern and invites a response to change. In Five of Cups, consider how this relates to grief.

Acceptance
Lingering Regret
Reconnection

Position: Present Time — Five of Cups reversed. In the period immediately surrounding today, acceptance, lingering regret, reconnection may describe what is active for you now.

Acceptance may be growing, or regret may be repeating without bringing new understanding. Reach toward the support that remains and let moving forward include, rather than erase, the loss.

Looking closer: A cloaked figure looks at three spilled cups while two stand behind, with a bridge nearby.
positions.lenses:
Tao / Wu Wei · Five of Cups

A practice of unforced attention with Five of Cups: What deserves mourning, and what support have I not yet turned toward?

Jungian interpretation · Five of Cups

Psychological lens: Attention can become fixed on absence. Integration makes room for loss within a larger life.
positions.positionContext: Position: Present Time — Five of Cups reversed. In the period immediately surrounding today, acceptance, lingering regret, reconnection may describe what is active for you now.

positions.label: Near Future · 3 Months
positions.meaning: what may develop over approximately the next three months if the present course continues
positions.original:
Original Card · Kn · Knight of Swords, reversed

Near Future · 3 Months

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Air · Swords
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Air · Swords · Air

Court rank: Knight

Knight is a court role, not a numbered pip card: an active way of pursuing the suit’s concerns, with both gifts and excesses. It can describe an approach or quality in anyone, without prescribing age or gender.

Recklessness
Argument
Tunnel Vision

Position: Near Future · 3 Months — Knight of Swords reversed. Over approximately the next three months, recklessness, argument, tunnel vision may show what develops if the present course continues; it is a direction, not a fixed prediction.

Urgency may be narrowing your judgement or making a conversation unnecessarily combative. Pause long enough to ask whether speed is helping the purpose you claim to serve.

Looking closer: A rider charges forward with a raised sword under a turbulent sky.
positions.lenses:
Tao / Wu Wei · Knight of Swords

A practice of unforced attention with Knight of Swords: Where do I need decisiveness, and where am I confusing urgency with certainty?

Jungian interpretation · Knight of Swords

Psychological lens: The wish to cut through difficulty can become rigid when thought loses contact with feeling and circumstance.

positions.original:
1 · THE ORIGINAL CARD IN THIS POSITION
Original Card · XII · The Hanged Man, reversed

You / Answer

CARD CORRESPONDENCE
Water
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Water · Water

Number: 12

Twelve marks a pause in the usual sequence and the possibility of a changed perspective. In The Hanged Man, consider how this relates to perspective.

Stagnation
Resistance
Needless Sacrifice

Position: You / Answer — The Hanged Man reversed. In a general reading, stagnation, resistance, needless sacrifice may describe where you stand now. If you asked a specific question, return to this card last and consider what answer it suggests for you.

Waiting may have lost its purpose, or a sacrifice may no longer serve anyone. Name what you are postponing and what would make the pause a conscious choice again.

Looking closer: A figure hangs by one foot with a calm face and a halo. Physical inversion becomes an image of changed perception rather than defeat.
positions.clar1:
2 · CLARIFIER 1 · HOW IT MODIFIES THE ORIGINAL CARD
Clarifier 1 · XVII · The Star, reversed

Hope may feel remote because you are tired or comparing your recovery with an ideal. Seek a reliable source of nourishment and notice small signs of connection before demanding confidence.

Astrology: Aquarius · Air

Number: 17

Seventeen opens a relationship with hope after the disruption of a former certainty. In The Star, consider how this relates to hope.

Looking closer: A kneeling figure pours water onto land and into a pool beneath a large star. Generosity and replenishment connect inner life with the wider world.

The Star (reversed) modifies The Hanged Man (reversed).

In You / Answer, the theme of discouragement and disconnection changes how stagnation and resistance may be expressed, rather than strengthening or opposing it.

Read this way because Water and Air are neutral to each other.

With both cards reversed, look at what is being held back or resisted.
positions.clar2:
3 · CLARIFIER 2 · HOW IT DEVELOPS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN BOTH
Clarifier 2 · II · Two of Cups, reversed

A relationship or agreement may be unequal or out of tune. Name the difference and assess whether repair is mutual rather than assuming one person can restore the connection alone.

Astrology: Water · Cups · Water

Number: 2

Two brings relationship, polarity and the need to consider another position. In Two of Cups, consider how this relates to mutuality.

Looking closer: Two people exchange cups beneath a winged lion and entwined staff.

Two of Cups (reversed) reinforces The Hanged Man (reversed) and modifies The Star (reversed).

In You / Answer, it adds a further angle: the theme of imbalance and disconnection shifts how stagnation (The Hanged Man) and discouragement (The Star) work together.

Read this way because with The Hanged Man: both are Water cards; with The Star: Air and Water are neutral to each other.

Because Two of Cups (reversed) is reversed, read what it adds as something still forming or held back. As a Minor Arcana card, Two of Cups brings the Major theme down to a practical, everyday expression in feelings and relationships.

Clarifier 2 was drawn because Clarifier 1 is also a Major Arcana card (Chas's teaching rule).

Surrounding Energies

Fire · Wands
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Dependence on Praise
Setback
Private Success

Looking closer: A rider crowned with a wreath carries a decorated wand among companions.

Hopes, Fears & Attitude

Earth · Pentacles
SKY AT THIS READING
No planetary placement assigned

Astrology: Earth · Pentacles · Earth

Court rank: Queen

Queen is a court role, not a numbered pip card: a receptive, sustaining expression of the suit’s qualities. It can describe an approach or quality in anyone, without prescribing age or gender.

Neglected Needs
Overfunctioning
Insecurity

You may be holding daily life together for everyone while becoming depleted yourself. Restore practical support and distinguish being caring from being endlessly available.

Looking closer: A queen holds a pentacle in a lush landscape with a rabbit nearby.
positions.lenses:
Tao / Wu Wei · Queen of Pentacles

Psychological lens: Nurturing becomes sustainable when the self is recognised as someone worthy of the same care it offers others.

Force

Pushing harder may conceal uncertainty about where you are going. Reconcile conflicting priorities, check whether the goal is still yours, and regain direction before demanding more speed.

THE GOLDEN THREAD
Read the spread as a whole

The Golden Thread follows 11 revealed cards across this reading, including every clarifier. Every card came up reversed and are read through their reversed meaning.

PAST · 18–24 MONTHS
The Moon, reversed + Three of Swords, reversed

The original The Moon, reversed highlights emerging clarity and confusion; Three of Swords, reversed introduces recovery and held resentment. Consider whether these energies support one another or ask for balance.

The astrological correspondences in dialogue are The Moon, reversed (Pisces) meets Three of Swords, reversed (Air · Swords). These may suggest qualities in yourself, a situation, or another person's influence; they do not establish someone's zodiac sign.

PRESENT TIME
Five of Cups, reversed

The foundation is acceptance and lingering regret; clarifiers can deepen this interpretation.

The astrological correspondences in dialogue are Five of Cups, reversed (Water · Cups). These may suggest qualities in yourself, a situation, or another person's influence; they do not establish someone's zodiac sign.

Knight of Swords, reversed

The foundation is recklessness and argument; clarifiers can deepen this interpretation.

The astrological correspondences in dialogue are Knight of Swords, reversed (Air · Swords). These may suggest qualities in yourself, a situation, or another person's influence; they do not establish someone's zodiac sign.

YOU / ANSWER
The Hanged Man, reversed + The Star, reversed + Two of Cups, reversed

The original The Hanged Man, reversed highlights stagnation and resistance; The Star, reversed introduces discouragement and disconnection; Two of Cups, reversed introduces imbalance and disconnection. Consider whether these energies support one another or ask for balance.

The astrological correspondences in dialogue are The Hanged Man, reversed (Water) meets The Star, reversed (Aquarius) meets Two of Cups, reversed (Water · Cups). These may suggest qualities in yourself, a situation, or another person's influence; they do not establish someone's zodiac sign.

SURROUNDING ENERGIES

The foundation is dependence on praise and setback; clarifiers can deepen this interpretation.

The astrological correspondences in dialogue are Six of Wands, reversed (Fire · Wands). These may suggest qualities in yourself, a situation, or another person's influence; they do not establish someone's zodiac sign.

Queen of Pentacles, reversed

The foundation is neglected needs and overfunctioning; clarifiers can deepen this interpretation.

The astrological correspondences in dialogue are Queen of Pentacles, reversed (Earth · Pentacles). These may suggest qualities in yourself, a situation, or another person's influence; they do not establish someone's zodiac sign.

OUTCOME · NEXT 18–24 MONTHS
The Chariot, reversed + Ace of Wands, reversed

The original The Chariot, reversed highlights drift and force; Ace of Wands, reversed introduces blocked spark and delay. Consider whether these energies support one another or ask for balance.

The astrological correspondences in dialogue are The Chariot, reversed (Cancer) meets Ace of Wands, reversed (Fire · Wands). These may suggest qualities in yourself, a situation, or another person's influence; they do not establish someone's zodiac sign.

FROM CARD TO CARD

The reading begins with The Moon, reversed in Past · 18–24 Months and moves toward The Chariot, reversed in Outcome · Next 18–24 Months.

Present Time · Five of Cups, reversed. Following The Moon, Five of Cups may draw your attention toward acceptance.

Near Future · 3 Months · Knight of Swords, reversed. Following Five of Cups, Knight of Swords may draw your attention toward recklessness.

You / Answer · The Hanged Man, reversed. Following Knight of Swords, The Hanged Man may draw your attention toward stagnation.

Surrounding Energies · Six of Wands, reversed. Following The Hanged Man, Six of Wands may draw your attention toward dependence on praise.

Hopes, Fears & Attitude · Queen of Pentacles, reversed. Following Six of Wands, Queen of Pentacles may draw your attention toward neglected needs.

Outcome · Next 18–24 Months · The Chariot, reversed. Following Queen of Pentacles, The Chariot may draw your attention toward drift.

The card-to-card movement is the heart of this reading: The Moon, reversed opens the question, and The Chariot, reversed shows where that pattern may be heading if the present choices continue.

Keep the part that speaks to your lived situation, and use the cards as a prompt for reflection and choice.

THE OVERALL INVITATION

Across these cards, emerging clarity, confusion, projection, recovery form the central pattern. Which part speaks to your present circumstances, and what choice might help you respond? This is a perspective, not a fixed prediction.

Numbers through your reading

The Moon (18) · Three of Swords (3) · Five of Cups (5) · Knight of Swords (Knight) · The Hanged Man (12) · The Star (17) · Two of Cups (2) · Six of Wands (6) · Queen of Pentacles (Queen) · The Chariot (7) · Ace of Wands (1). Their numbered cards sum to 71, reducing to 8. No opening dice were rolled for this reading.

These numbers are symbolic prompts, not guarantees. Notice whether any patterns resonate with numbers personally meaningful to you.

Take what resonates, and leave the rest.
